title: Johnson transformation for a list of numbers (forward: original scale to transformed scale)
label2: Type in one or more numeric values (comma-separated) to be transformed using the Johnson transformation function
inputNumbers: Type in one or more numeric values separated by commas (e.g. 47.5, 50.2, 53.6)
useStoredRad: Option 1: Use the Johnson type and parameters stored with a variable from the dataset (jtrans_* attributes from a prior Johnson transformation)
variableSelcted: Select a variable with stored Johnson transformation parameters
manualParamsRad: Option 2: Manually specify the Johnson transformation type and parameters (e.g. from Minitab output)
lambda: Lambda (λ) - must be greater than 0 for SB and SU. May be left blank for SL (not used, defaults to 1)
digits: Digits - rounds to the specified number of decimal places

help.title: Johnson transformation for a list of numbers
help.body:
Description
Apply the Johnson transformation (forward direction: original scale to transformed scale) to one or more user-supplied numeric values. The transformation type (SB, SL, or SU) and the parameters Gamma (γ), Eta (η), Epsilon (ε), Lambda (λ) are obtained from either a variable with stored Johnson attributes or manually entered

This is useful for transforming specification limits, targets, or any reference values using the same Johnson function that was fitted to a dataset - for example, before running a capability analysis on the transformed scale, or to check what a particular original-scale value maps to in the transformed space

The three Johnson transformation functions
SB (bounded): Y = γ + η * Ln( (X - ε) / (λ + ε - X) )
The input X must satisfy ε < X < ε + λ (the bounded range). Values outside this range cannot be transformed and will be flagged

SL (lognormal): Y = γ + η * Ln( X - ε )
The input X must satisfy X > ε. Values at or below ε cannot be transformed

SU (unbounded): Y = γ + η * Asinh( (X - ε) / λ )
Any real-valued X is accepted (the SU family is unbounded)

For reference - Minitab SB function notation
Minitab prints the SB function with the upper bound written out, e.g. 0.8046 + 0.8937 * Ln( ( X - 46.2931 ) / ( 59.8636 - X ) ) - the second constant inside the Ln is λ + ε, so λ = 59.8636 - 46.2931 = 13.5706
